findings.claim: The QA route drives the one-paragraph hands-on instructions beginning at html-css-js/html-and-css/flexbox/artifact.html:252, but neither the route nor the artifact presents each task as numbered where-to-look, what-to-type-or-press, what-to-expect, and how-to-know-done steps. The current route can therefore pass while the captain-required instruction shape is absent.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite each hands-on task as an accessible numbered list with explicit where, action, expected result, and done criterion, without exposing the reasoning answer; update the QA path to assert that structure while retaining the same behavioral route.

findings.claim: The manifest records modeledWorstPath as modeledP50 + 2.50 minutes, while the review direction fixes this module route at modeledP50 + 2.0. The result is conservative and remains under 15 minutes, but it does not use the required model.
findings.recommendation: Recalculate modeledWorstPath as modeledP50 + 2.0, update the basis text, and derive budget/aboutLabel from that corrected value without exceeding the 15-minute ceiling.

findings.claim: “Leftover space is the container’s width minus all the bases” is presented as the general Flexbox rule. The real algorithm uses the container’s inner main size, outer hypothetical main sizes, margins, gaps and min/max clamping; automatic minimum sizes can also prevent the simple basis arithmetic.

evidence.section: 1.1 Overview and 9.7 Resolving Flexible Lengths: multi-line flex containers remain one-dimensional; free-space resolution uses outer hypothetical main sizes, constraints and scaled shrink factors

findings.recommendation: Label the arithmetic as a simplified case with no padding, border, gap, margins or min/max constraints, as already true of the worked examples. Say that real flex sizing additionally accounts for those values and constraints.
